summary: Completed backend+frontend proxy validation for local Express /api forwarding, real browser consulting/admin flows through route.fetch forwarding, and protocol-level proxy hardening checks.

minor.issue: Returns JSON 404 while GET /api/ returns JSON 200; proxy path handling is consistent API-side, but root API behavior differs by trailing slash.

action_items: Decide whether /api should match /api/ (currently /api=404 and /api/=200) and normalize if required by product/API contract.
Owner must still apply frontend Render deployment/runtime config changes in production; workspace verification does not itself change live Render service wiring.
critical_code_review_comments: apiProxy.js safeguards are active: untrusted Forwarded/X-Forwarded headers are stripped, security headers in Connection are rejected, malformed API paths are rejected with JSON 400, and upstream connection failures return redacted JSON 502.
Root-mounted proxy is functioning before static/security HTML pipeline for API routes in this workspace runtime.
No backend/form/UI source files were modified during this test iteration; only new test/report artifacts were added.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (desktop+mobile consulting submit via forwarded proxy, duplicate guard 409, and admin login/verify/logout via forwarded proxy passed)

seed_data_creation: Created two uniquely labelled QA consulting records (desktop/mobile) and removed only exact created IDs during cleanup.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Browser tests were run against external preview URL while intercepting only preview /api requests and forwarding them to local Express proxy at http://127.0.0.1:3000 via route.fetch+route.fulfill; forwarding counters confirmed proxy usage (consulting: 6 each run, admin: 11). Real consulting POST returned 201 on desktop+mobile; duplicate replay returned 409; DB count remained one per email; exact cleanup executed. External checks also confirmed /api/definitely-not-real => 404 JSON and /media-kit => 404 HTML.
rca of the issue: Trailing-slash route mismatch: backend/proxy chain serves /api/ but not /api. This is not an HTML fallback leak (both are API responses), but a contract inconsistency likely caused by backend route registration expecting slash-form root while security/proxy path allowlist includes both variants.
